topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system, acknowledges its reputation for complex nomenclature, and frames the scope of the lecture.

topics.label: Core principles and central mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, nomenclature rules, and central role of component C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways of complement activation and how they converge to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary immune outcomes mediated by activated complement, including opsonization, inflammation, and pathogen lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host tissue protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical pathology of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct medical consequences and disease manifestations resulting from deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement defenses
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how pathogens, exemplified by Staphylococcus aureus, employ specialized mechanisms to subvert complement-mediated clearance.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming topics
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion on complement and previews the topic for the subsequent lecture.
